evals.prompt: All the audits on evals/files/sample-repo are done. Put together the final audit report for the Digital Inventory launch decision.
evals.expected_output: build_report.py is run and audit/audit-report.md is produced. The executive summary recommends NO-GO because a Critical (AUTHZ-001) and a High (AUTHZ-002, merged with AUTHZ-003) are open, with a caveat naming the skipped secrets audit, lists AUTHZ-001, AUTHZ-002 and HDR-001 as the top three risks in plain language, the scope table shows the skipped secrets audit with its reason, the pass/fail matrix marks authz FAIL, headers WARN, frontend best practices PASS and secrets NOT RUN, the remediation plan lists AUTHZ-001 and AUTHZ-002 as must-fix-before-launch and HDR-001/HDR-002 as post-launch tickets, and FEBP-002 appears only in the false-positive appendix.
expectations: The executive summary states a NO-GO recommendation
A caveat listed after the recommendation names the skipped audit-secrets-and-config
The executive summary's top three risks start with AUTHZ-001 (the only Critical) and do not contain CWE ids
The 'Must fix before launch' table contains AUTHZ-001 and AUTHZ-002 and nothing of Medium or lower severity
AUTHZ-003 is merged into AUTHZ-002 (shown as merged, both locations listed in Appendix A) and does not appear as a separate finding
HDR-001 and HDR-002 appear under 'Ticket for post-launch'
The pass/fail matrix shows authz and access control as FAIL, security headers as WARN, frontend best practices as PASS and secrets and config as NOT RUN
FEBP-002 is listed only in the excluded false positives appendix and is not counted
The OWASP/ASVS section embeds the mapper's Top 10 table
The scope table shows the skipped secrets audit with its reason
Appendix B lists the scripts from the status files and the endpoint_probe.txt evidence file

evals.prompt: Can you export the audit report for evals/files/sample-repo as a Word document? The client wants a .docx.
evals.expected_output: build_report.py is run with --docx. If pandoc is installed, audit/audit-report.docx is produced; if not, the reply says pandoc was not found, gives the install pointer and the exact pandoc command, and delivers audit/audit-report.md. The status file records the export outcome.
expectations: If pandoc is missing the reply says so explicitly and gives the pandoc command rather than silently skipping

evals.prompt: is this thing ready to ship? summarise the audits in evals/files/sample-repo for me in a couple of lines and tell me what has to be fixed first
evals.expected_output: A short plain-language answer derived from the generated report: not ready (NO-GO); the unauthenticated company-admin endpoints must be fixed first, then the missing ownership filter in the base repository (covers orders and invoices); HSTS and nosniff can be ticketed for after launch; the secrets audit did not run so that area is unknown.
expectations: Answer says the application is not ready (NO-GO) and explains why in plain language
Answer names the unauthenticated admin endpoints as the first fix and the ownership filter as the second
Answer mentions that the secrets audit was skipped so that area is unverified
Answer distinguishes launch blockers from post-launch items
